info.title: SKU.io — Map Supplier Costs onto Reorderable Products
info.description: Fill in missing supplier costs for reorderable products from the user's supplier price lists or past purchase orders, after approval. Use for the Launch Roadmap's "Supplier costs" step or products with no supplier pricing. For a new price file on products that have costs, use update-catalog-pricing.

get.summary: Catalog health counts, including products_with_supplier, products_without_supplier, products_with_non_zero_supplier_price and products_with_zero_supplier_price.

Bulk-read the catalog. Rows include sku, name, type, archived_at, unit_cost, default_supplier_id, default_supplier_name, default_supplier_sku and default_supplier_price. filter[supplier_price.is_empty]=1 narrows to products whose default supplier link has no price (or that have no default supplier at all).

get.summary: A product's supplier links, each with supplier_sku, is_default and its pricing tiers (tier name and price). This is where the account's real tier name comes from, and it shows prices on non-default suppliers that the list filter can't see.
Resolve a supplier named on a price list to its supplier id.

get.summary: The most recent non-draft purchase order line for the product with a price above zero: { amount, purchase_order_id, purchase_order_date }, or data null when it was never bought.
Read the purchase order behind a last purchase price, to learn which supplier it was bought from and in what currency before proposing it as that supplier's cost.

put.summary: Write a supplier cost onto one product. Send only suppliers[], with operation "updateOrCreate" on every entry so no other supplier link is touched. Creates the supplier link when the product has none for that supplier.

suppliers.description: Each { supplier_id, operation: "updateOrCreate", pricing: [{ supplier_pricing_tier_name, price }], supplier_sku (optional), is_default (optional, only for a product with no default supplier) }. price is numeric, >= 0 and < 100000. An unknown tier name CREATES a new tier, so use a name read from get-product-suppliers.
